## What this video is for

We are doing one thing: getting four programs onto your laptop, making your own copy of
the course workspace, and running a file that proves it all works.

**Work along with me, do not watch first and do it later.** Pause whenever you need to and
rewind anything that goes past too fast. Nothing here is a race, and the video will wait.

## What you will have at the end

[Project Setup · 25 points · due Friday, September 11]{.eyebrow}

- R, VS Code, Quarto, and Git installed and answering
- Your own repository on GitHub, named `mc451-workspace`
- That folder open in VS Code on your laptop

## Something is going to break

- It breaks in every section, every semester, for somebody
- It is never because that person is bad at this
- It is one version number disagreeing with another
- **Pause the video the moment something looks wrong.** Do not push on and hope.

## Install 1 of 4: R

**What it is:** the language that does the counting and the statistics.

Download from [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org). Take the newest release for
your operating system and accept every default.

**On a Mac you have to pick the right file:** Apple silicon or Intel. Apple menu, **About
This Mac**, and read the chip.

**Start this download now**, then keep watching. It is the biggest of the four.

## Install 2 of 4: VS Code

**What it is:** the window you will actually work in. It is a text editor, free, from
Microsoft.

Download from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com). Accept every default.

**On a Mac**, open the downloaded file and drag **Visual Studio Code** into Applications.
Do not run it out of the Downloads window.

Your writing, your code, and your results all live here, so you stop switching between
five programs to do one thing.

## Install 3 of 4: Quarto

**What it is:** the thing that turns your file into a finished document.

Download from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started). Accept
every default.

You write prose and code in one file, press render, and get back a document with the
charts and numbers already dropped into place.

## Install 4 of 4: Git

**What it is:** the program that keeps a history of your files, so nothing you write this
semester can be lost.

**Windows:** download from [git-scm.com/downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads). The
installer asks a lot of questions. **Next** is the right answer to every one of them.

**Mac:** nothing to download. In Terminal type `git --version`. If a box offers to install
developer tools, click **Install** and wait. That box is Git arriving.

## Prove all four are really there

Installers fail quietly. Open VS Code, then **Terminal, New Terminal**, and run these two:

```bash
quarto check
git --version
```

`quarto check` is Quarto's own self test. It checks itself, then goes looking for R, and
prints a line for each thing it finds.

**You should see:** green check marks from `quarto check`, and a version number from Git.

**Windows only:** typing `R --version` says "not recognized" even when R is perfectly fine,
because the R installer does not add R to the command line. On a Mac it answers normally.
Either way, `quarto check` is the check that counts.

## Step 1: make your own copy of the workspace

A **repository**, or repo, is just a folder that Git is watching. Ours has the course
folder structure already in it.

Go to [github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-workspace](https://github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-workspace).

- Click the green **Use this template**, then **Create a new repository**
- Name it `mc451-workspace`. Leave it **Public**.
- Click **Create repository**

**You should see:** the same folders, now under your own username.

## Step 2: bring it down to your laptop

Nothing is on your computer yet. Only on GitHub.

- On your new repo, click the green **Code** button and copy the URL
- In VS Code press `Ctrl+Shift+P`, or `Cmd+Shift+P` on a Mac. A search bar drops down.
- Type **Git: Clone**, press Enter, paste the URL
- Pick a folder you will find again. `Documents/MC451/` is a fine answer.
- When VS Code asks, click **Open**

**You should see:** your folder names down the left side of VS Code.

## Step 3: let VS Code install the extensions

A box appears in the bottom right: **"This workspace has extension recommendations."**

Click **Install All**. That is Quarto, R, and GitLens, and it means everyone in the course
is working in the same environment.

If the box already vanished, press `Ctrl+Shift+X` and search for **Quarto** and for **R**
by REditorSupport. Stuck? [Install VS Code](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/install-vscode.html)

## Step 4: open the file we wrote for you

Download it here, or from the blue button on the
[Resources page](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/index.html):

[aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/starters/00-check-your-setup.qmd](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/starters/00-check-your-setup.qmd)

Save it into your `mc451-workspace` folder, then open it in VS Code.

You do not have to write it. You do not have to understand it. You click through it one
grey box at a time, and it tells you what each box should print.

**Pause here and work through the whole file.** The rest of this video assumes you have.

## What "working" looks like

The file finishes by running a checker we wrote for this course:

```r
library(v2v)
setup()
```

**You want:** green check marks all the way down **Required R packages**.

**Red next to Quarto or Git** is fine if you have not reached those steps yet.

**Red under Required** is the one that needs me. Email me that whole block of output,
exactly as it appears, rather than describing it.

## When it breaks

- **`quarto: command not found`.** That terminal opened before Quarto finished installing.
  Close it, open a new one. This is the single most common problem in the whole setup.
- **`there is no package called 'v2v'`.** R is fine, the package is not there yet. Rerun
  the install step inside the check file.
- **Red text in R is not automatically an error.** R prints ordinary progress in red. Read
  the last line, not the colour.
- **GitHub asks for a password and refuses it.** Not your mistake. It wants a token now.
  Click through VS Code's sign-in and it never asks again.

## Checkpoint

Every line should be true before you stop:

- `quarto check` comes back clean, and `git --version` answers
- Your own `mc451-workspace` exists on GitHub, and is cloned into VS Code
- The extensions installed
- `00-check-your-setup.qmd` runs and `setup()` comes back green

If any line is not true, do not leave it there. Email me the exact wording of the error,
or bring the laptop to office hours. Closing the laptop and hoping is the one approach
that never works.
